title: Currency Calculator Quest
welcome_lead: A British holidaymaker in New York, a French car shipped to London. Convert currencies and balance the trade books.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics calculations adventure on exchange rates, trade balances and global trade arithmetic.
final_note: Currency conversion conquered. On to exam-style global stretch!

concepts.def: Currency rises in value vs others.
Currency falls in value vs others.

walkthroughs.body_html: Rule: multiply when going from pounds to foreign; divide when coming back. Example: £200 × 1.20 = $240. To go back: $240 ÷ 1.20 = £200. Always double-check by reversing.
UK exports £450bn, imports £520bn. Trade balance = 450 − 520 = −£70bn deficit. A persistent deficit can weaken the £ over time as more pounds are sold to buy foreign currency for imports.

If £1 falls from $1.30 to $1.10, UK goods are 15% cheaper to American buyers — exports likely rise. But imported petrol and food cost more pounds — inflation rises. Evaluation: depends on PED of exports/imports.
